payload.text:
**Summarizing container setup and concerns**

I need to analyze the container setup, noting that both services share the same container_name and only one profile is used. The ETH mining service is outdated since Ethereum moved past PoW, and the pool requires a wallet address entry. The API is exposed on 0.0.0.0 without volumes or restart policies. The AMD device uses /dev/dri and might require privileged mode; NVIDIA needs a runtime, and Compose v3.9 deploy settings only work with swarm, meaning reservations are ignored by docker-compose. I'll highlight these issues and offer suggestions for improvement.

Aquí tienes un análisis del `docker-compose.yml` que compartiste.

Lo que hace
- Define dos servicios: `lolminer-amd` y `lolminer-nvidia`, ambos construyen la imagen desde `Dockerfile` en el mismo directorio.
- Ambos lanzan `lolMiner` con parámetros predefinidos (pool 2miners, wallet, API host/port).
- Usa `profiles` para elegir AMD o NVIDIA al levantar.

Hallazgos/observaciones clave
- Solo se puede ejecutar uno a la vez: ambos usan `container_name: lolminer`, así que si intentas correr ambos perfiles, chocan.
- `deploy.resources.reservations` solo aplica en Swarm; con `docker-compose` clásico se ignora. Para NVIDIA en compose necesitas `runtime`/`device_requests` según tu versión.
- El `entrypoint` apunta a ETH PoW (`--coin ETH`). Ethereum ya no es minable por PoW, así que esto no funcionará hoy; habría que cambiar coin/pool si el objetivo es minar otra moneda.
- El `--apihost 0.0.0.0` expone la API a toda la red del contenedor; si se publica el puerto en el host, quedaría expuesto. No hay protección/autenticación.
- El wallet está hardcodeado. Si es de ejemplo, bien; si no, es una fuga de datos/credenciales.

Sugerencias prácticas
- Cambiar `container_name` por valores distintos o eliminarlo.
- Para NVIDIA en compose no-Swarm, usar `deploy` no basta; configura `device_requests` o `runtime: nvidia` (según tu stack).
- Reemplazar coin/pool a uno vigente (p. ej. ETC, KAS, etc.) y ajustar `--user`.
- Añadir `restart: unless-stopped` y variables via `environment`/`.env` en lugar de hardcodear.
- Si usas la API, restringirla a `127.0.0.1` o a una red interna.

Si quieres, dime tu objetivo (minería real, prueba local, benchmarking, etc.) y te propongo un compose ajustado.

Sí, es posible usar ese `docker-compose` como base de idea, pero no tal cual. Lo importante para mantener la autoconversión a BTC de NiceHash es **minar contra los stratum de NiceHash usando tu dirección BTC de NiceHash como usuario**. El compose que viste mina ETH en 2miners, así que hay que cambiar pool/coin/usuario.

Puntos clave:
- NiceHash paga en BTC siempre que apuntes al pool de NiceHash con tu **dirección BTC de NiceHash** (lo que ya tienes en `k8s/miners/nicehash/secret.yaml`).
- Necesitas elegir **algoritmo** (p. ej. ETCHash, KawPow, etc.) y **región** (EU/US) y configurar el pool de NiceHash correspondiente.
- `lolMiner` funciona, pero el comando debe apuntar a NiceHash (`--pool ... --user <BTC>.<worker> --pass x`).
- El `docker-compose` usa `ETH` PoW y 2miners; eso no sirve para NiceHash hoy.

Si quieres, puedo preparar el reemplazo del Deployment en `k8s/miners/nicehash/` usando `lolMiner` (o el minero que prefieras) y mantener `MINING_ADDRESS`/`MINING_WORKER_NAME`. Solo necesito:
1) Tipo de GPU en ese nodo (NVIDIA/AMD).  
2) Algoritmo/moneda que quieres minar en NiceHash (o si prefieres “lo más rentable”).  
3) Región de NiceHash (EU/USA/etc.).  

Con eso te dejo el manifiesto listo para aplicar.

{"result":"# Miners: XMRig (Unmineable) deployment notes

## Context
Deployment lives in `k8s/miners/unmineable/` and uses the prebuilt image `thechristech/unmineable:latest`. We override the image entrypoint via ConfigMap to control runtime behavior without rebuilding the image.

## Key files
- `k8s/miners/unmineable/deployment.yaml`: Deployment, mounts `/usr/src/mining/entrypoint.sh` from ConfigMap, sets env vars, requests/limits.
- `k8s/miners/unmineable/configmap-script.yaml`: Provides the custom entrypoint script.
- `k8s/miners/unmineable/configmap.yaml`: User-facing env config (pool/coin/worker/threads/affinity).
- `k8s/miners/unmineable/secret.yaml`: Wallet address.

## Why entrypoint override
The upstream image includes `entrypoint.sh` and `config/xmrig.json`. We override only the entrypoint to:
- remove CPU_LIMIT_* logic,
- keep control of pool/coin/wallet via env,
- add explicit thread control (`MINING_THREADS`) and RandomX init threads to match,
- add optional CPU affinity for P‑cores.
We do NOT mount/override `xmrig.json` because it is read-only if mounted from a ConfigMap and upstream uses `sed -i` to replace placeholders.

## Current entrypoint behavior (ConfigMap)
- Accepts `POOL` (and optional fallback to `MINING_POOL`), `COIN`, `REFERRAL_CODE`, `WALLET_ADDRESS`, `WORKER_NAME`.
- If `MINING_THREADS` set, adds `--threads=$MINING_THREADS --randomx-init=$MINING_THREADS`.
- If `CPU_AFFINITY_MASK` set, adds `--cpu-affinity=$CPU_AFFINITY_MASK`.
- Runs XMRig in foreground via `exec`, with either `-c xmrig.json` or CLI params (default path uses CLI params).

## Hasrate improvement findings
Main gain came from:
1) Limiting threads to P‑cores only (avoid E‑cores),
2) Setting explicit thread count via `MINING_THREADS`,
3) Adding CPU affinity via `CPU_AFFINITY_MASK`.

On the i9‑13980HX node, P‑cores are CPUs `0-15`. Using only one thread per P‑core yields:
- `MINING_THREADS=8`
- `CPU_AFFINITY_MASK=0x5555` (CPUs 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14)

Result: ~5.1–5.2 kH/s with 8 threads (RandomX), notably higher than 12 threads across mixed cores (~2.9–3.0 kH/s).

## Current config values
- `k8s/miners/unmineable/configmap.yaml`
  - `MINING_THREADS: "8"`
  - `CPU_AFFINITY_MASK: "0x5555"`

## Notes on CPU Manager
Attempted to enable `cpuManagerPolicy=static` via k3s; kubelet crashed because reserved CPU resources were not configured. This change was reverted. The affinity mask still works without `static`, but does not guarantee exclusive cores.

## Huge pages & MSR
Managed by Ansible role `common`:
- `vm.nr_hugepages` is set via sysctl (RandomX requirement).
- `msr` kernel module is loaded for RandomX optimizations.

## Runtime validation
Logs should show:
- `Threads manually set to: 8`
- `CPU affinity mask set to: 0x5555`
- `randomx init dataset ... (8 threads)`
- `cpu ... profile * (8 threads)`
- `READY threads 8/8`
- `DONATE 0%`

## Deployment apply (manual)
```
kubectl apply --validate=false \
  -f k8s/miners/unmineable/configmap.yaml \
  -f k8s/miners/unmineable/configmap-script.yaml \
  -f k8s/miners/unmineable/secret.yaml \
  -f k8s/miners/unmineable/deployment.yaml
```
"}

# lolminer-docker
Tried to make it as simple as possible to run [lolminer](https://github.com/Lolliedieb/lolMiner-releases) without worrying about
drivers or the mining software (at least on amd). The docker images are named as follows:
`ubuntu<ubuntu-version>-<cuda/amd-version>-<lolminer version>`. For instance:
`ubuntu22.04-cuda-11.7.1-1.84` or `ubuntu22.04-amd-21.30-1.84`

## amd:
Tested with Ubuntu 20.04 and 20.10 host operating systems without any special
drivers installed on the host OS (ie, don't need to worry about the mess of
AMD drivers in the most recent Ubuntu OS's).

For physical hardware, tested with rx580, rx480 gpus.

https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/compscidr/lolminer-docker
From dockerhub:
```
docker run --device=/dev/dri:/dev/dri compscidr/lolminer-docker:ubuntu22.04-amd-21.30-1.84 <insert lolminer args>
```

For instance:
```
docker run --device=/dev/dri:/dev/dri compscidr/lolminer-docker:ubuntu22.04-amd-21.30-1.84--coin ETH --pool eth.2miners.com --port 2020 --user 0x74ba897f65f04008d8eff364efcc54b0a20e17eb.amd-docker --apihost 0.0.0.0 --apiport 4069
```

The only fees are the lolminer fees, I didn't add any additional fees.

## nvidia:
On the host, you need a bit more work to get the nvidia docker runtime (only required once):
```
distribution=$(. /etc/os-release;echo $ID$VERSION_ID)
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | sudo apt-key add -
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list

sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
sudo systemctl restart docker
```

Then you can run as follows:
```
docker run --gpus all compscidr/lolminer-docker:ubuntu22.04-cuda-11.7.1-1.84 --coin ETH --pool eth.2miners.com --port 2020 --user 0x74ba897f65f04008d8eff364efcc54b0a20e17eb.nvidia-docker --apihost 0.0.0.0 --apiport 4069
```

Confirmed working with a ubuntu20.04 host and an nvidia rtx 3080 gpu. On a fresh
Ubuntu 20.04 install, cuda 11.4.2 image will work, however if you've got
a newer version on your host for some other reason, you can bump to a newer cuda
version in the image as well if you want. You can check your cuda version and
gpu driver version with `nvidia-smi`

## docker-compose
Alternatively you can use the provided docker-compose file which will build
everything from source. You will want to update the `entrypoint` within the
docker-compose.yml file to use your own wallet and arguments for lolminer.

Then for AMD:
`docker-compose --profile amd up`

and for Nvidia:
`docker-compose --profile nvidia up`

payload.text:
**Investigating GPU compatibility issues**

I'm examining why the GPU is detected but marked inactive for KASPA mining in lolMiner 1.84. It might be due to unsupported algorithm, driver or runtime mismatches, or lolMiner version limitations for newer GPUs like the RTX 4070. To diagnose, I plan to create a temporary GPU-enabled pod using `kubectl run` with runtimeClassName and GPU limits, then exec inside to run commands like `lolMiner --list-devices` and `--benchmark KASPA` to check device compatibility and miner behavior. If version 1.84 lacks support, building a custom image with lolMiner 1.96a could be needed to enable KASPA on this hardware.

If version 1.84 lacks support, building a custom image with lolMiner 1.96a could be needed to enable KASPA on this hardware.

No puedo “probar Heavyhash‑Karlsen” en NiceHash: **NiceHash no ofrece ese algoritmo**. Lo verifiqué con su API pública y no aparece Karlsen/Heavyhash‑Karlsen; además, ninguno de los hostnames típicos (`karlsenhash.*`, `heavyhash-karlsen.*`) resuelve en DNS.

Dos opciones reales:
1) Mantener NiceHash y usar **KHEAVYHASH (Kaspa)**, pero cambiar el puerto al oficial **3395** (según API).  
2) Si quieres **Karlsen**, entonces no puede ser NiceHash (no hay stratum). Tendrías que minar en otro pool y perder la auto‑conversión a BTC de NiceHash.

Además, con lolMiner 1.81/1.84 el GPU queda “incompatible” para KASPA en tu 4070 Laptop (mensaje: *All devices deselected or failed compatibility check*). Eso apunta a falta de soporte del kernel en esa build; habría que:
- usar un **miner distinto** (Rigel/BzMiner), o
- **construir** una imagen con lolMiner más nuevo (1.96a) y probar.

2) Cambie de miner para KASPA en NiceHash, o

    "body": "## Changes\r\n\r\n- Added support for mining Cuckaroo-29 as used for Tari for all Nvidia GTX 1000 cards and newer as well as AMD RX 400 cards and newer with at least 6G of memory. El problema real no es el pool ni el puerto: **lolMiner en esa imagen no soporta KASPA/HeavyHash en tu RTX 4070 Laptop**. Por eso el log termina en `All devices deselected or failed compatiblity check` aunque ya conecta y autoriza al pool.

Intenté “investigar en la comunidad”, pero:
- Las búsquedas públicas están detrás de captcha o sin contenido útil sin login.
- Los issues accesibles no mencionan Ada/4070+KASPA de forma directa.

Así que, sin una fuente clara, la solución práctica es:
1) **Usar un miner que sí soporte KASPA en Ada** (Rigel/BzMiner) y mantener NiceHash, o  
2) **Construir una imagen con lolMiner más nuevo** (>=1.96) y probar.

Dime cuál prefieres y lo hago.

payload.message: de lo que sobra, cual es la opinion sobre posibilidad de ganancia con GPU?

En NiceHash, con una sola GPU laptop, la “ganancia” suele ser baja y muy variable. En general:

- **KHEAVYHASH (Kaspa)** suele ser de los más rentables en NiceHash, pero en lolMiner 1.81 no te funciona en esta GPU.
- **ETHASH/ETCHASH** normalmente son de las menos rentables hoy.
- **AUTOLYKOS2, BEAM‑III, FLUX (ZelHash), EQUIHASH, NEXA** pueden dar algo, pero suelen estar por debajo de KHEAVYHASH y dependen mucho del precio/mercado del momento.

La mejor respuesta real es medir hashrate y contrastarlo con el precio en NiceHash (calculadora o API). Si quieres, corro benchmarks rápidos en tu GPU para los algoritmos que quedan y te doy estimaciones.

import json, urllib.request

pay=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(pay_url))['miningAlgorithms']

pay_map={a['algorithm']:a for a in pay}

    # NiceHash docs: paying is in BTC per unit of displayed mining factor per day

    rows.append((a, info['title'], info['displayMiningFactor'], paying, btc_per_h))

rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[4], reverse=True)
for a,title,unit,paying,btc_per_h in rows:

- name: NVIDIA GPU host setup
  tags: ["nvidia", "gpu", "nvidia-host"]
  block:
    - name: Ensure pciutils installed for lspci
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: pciutils
        state: present
        update_cache: true
        cache_valid_time: 3600
    - name: Detect NVIDIA GPU (Vendor ID 10de)
      ansible.builtin.command: lspci -nm
      register: nvidia_gpu_lspci_out
      changed_when: false
    - name: Set GPU detected fact
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        nvidia_gpu_detected: "{{ '10de' in nvidia_gpu_lspci_out.stdout }}"
    - name: Abort if no NVIDIA GPU found
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "No NVIDIA GPU (Vendor ID 10de) detected on this host."
      when:
        - not nvidia_gpu_detected
        - not ansible_check_mode
    - name: Install driver tools
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - ubuntu-drivers-common
          - linux-headers-generic
          - software-properties-common
        state: present
    - name: Detect NVIDIA driver
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -o pipefail
        ubuntu-drivers devices 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'driver\s+:\s+\K(nvidia-driver-\d+)(?=\s.*recommended)'
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      register: nvidia_gpu_detected_driver
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false
      when: nvidia_gpu_driver_package == "auto"
    - name: Set detected driver
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        nvidia_gpu_driver_target: "{{ nvidia_gpu_detected_driver.stdout | trim }}"
      when:
        - nvidia_gpu_driver_package == "auto"
        - nvidia_gpu_detected_driver.stdout | length > 0
    - name: Set driver fallback
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        nvidia_gpu_driver_target: "{{ nvidia_gpu_driver_fallback }}"
      when:
        - nvidia_gpu_driver_package == "auto"
        - >-
          (nvidia_gpu_detected_driver.skipped is defined and
          nvidia_gpu_detected_driver.skipped) or
          (nvidia_gpu_detected_driver.stdout | length == 0)
    - name: Set manual driver
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        nvidia_gpu_driver_target: "{{ nvidia_gpu_driver_package }}"
      when: nvidia_gpu_driver_package != "auto"
    - name: Blacklist nouveau driver
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-nouveau.conf
        content: |
          blacklist nouveau
          options nouveau modeset=0
        mode: "0644"
      register: nvidia_gpu_blacklist_nouveau
    - name: Update initramfs if blacklist changed # noqa: no-handler
      ansible.builtin.command: update-initramfs -u
      when: nvidia_gpu_blacklist_nouveau.changed
      changed_when: true
      # Deriva el paquete nvidia-utils del driver detectado (ej: nvidia-driver-535 -> nvidia-utils-535)
    - name: Calculate nvidia-utils package name
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:

    - name: Check if NVIDIA packages are in broken state # noqa: command-instead-of-module

        apt-get purge -y 'nvidia-*' 'libnvidia-*' || true

      when: nvidia_gpu_broken_check.stdout | int > 0
